correctness.rationale: For \(d\ge3\), pairwise-zero products of the generator images force the induced cotangent matrix to have at most one nonzero entry per row, hence to be monomial. After the branch permutation is fixed, an off-principal component on branch \(j\) annihilates a valuation-one element of \(k[x_j]/(x_j^d)\), so it lies in the one-dimensional annihilator \(k x_j^{d-1}\). This yields the unique normal form. The shear subgroup is additive, branch substitutions form \(J_d(k)^n\), and permutations split the quotient. The \(d=2\) case is exactly \(\operatorname{GL}_n(k)\) because the maximal ideal squares to zero. Exhaustive prime-field checks match the formula.

value.rationale: The quotient is a canonical finite truncation of the Stanley--Reisner algebra of isolated vertices. The theorem gives a complete symmetry classification across all fields, identifies a sharp structural change from \(\operatorname{GL}_n\) at square-zero depth to a solvable identity component with symmetric component group at depth at least three, and yields an exact finite-field order for every prime power. This is a natural structural invariant of a standard family, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
